key_insight: Readily available smartphones can provide low-cost mechanical excitation for ultrasound elastography, with preliminary phantom reconstructions similar to those obtained using a dedicated actuator.
engineering_relevance: Smartphone excitation could reduce hardware costs and simplify integration of tissue-stiffness imaging systems.
method: Use a smartphone to induce mechanical excitation in a tissue-mimicking phantom.
Image the induced tissue displacements with ultrasound.
Solve the elasticity inverse problem using a finite element method.
evidence_signal: Preliminary tissue-mimicking phantom tests produced elasticity reconstructions described as similar to those obtained with a dedicated harmonic actuator, without quantitative metrics in the abstract.
watch_item: Feasibility is demonstrated only in preliminary phantom tests; clinical accuracy and excitation reproducibility remain unestablished.
paper_title: Ultrasound Elastography: Excitation Methods and Low-Cost Alternative
